intended_claim: Task0 shaping lowers neighborhood sensitivity and enlarges empirical damage tolerance, enabling future learning to move through less damaging directions and improve retention without sacrificing plasticity.
overall_verdict: The complete causal and split-robust chain is not supported. Narrow train-sample sensitivity and historical full-sequence endpoint-segment observations are supported, while A and B-test provide direct counterevidence to the proposed accuracy and generalization links.
what_results_support: A is an auditable package-level comparison of two inherited Task0 states under the same future SGD+EWC Task1 procedure and matched recorded randomness.
For seed0 and the chosen effective-weight coordinates, the GAM Task0 anchor has lower train256 raw empirical-Fisher trace and lower sampled train-neighborhood G and Q95 at all six nonzero radii.
In the historical GAM-to-GAM sequence, Task0 test-local CE damage is lower and effective-weight displacement is larger than in SGD-to-SGD at every Task1-Task9 endpoint.
At Task9, the GAM endpoint chord has lower S_path and D_subset, with passed quadrature and same-sample bound checks.
what_results_dont_support: A pure Task0-geometry effect independent of the inherited old head and EWC Fisher
Improved a21, a22, or two-task class-IL mean from inheriting the GAM Task0 package under future SGD+EWC
Lower test-neighborhood mean positive damage or generally larger test tolerance radii
A Hessian-flatness claim or reparameterization-invariant geometry
An optimization-trajectory integral; C measures endpoint straight segments
Causal mediation from Task0 shaping through sensitivity to later accuracy
missing_evidence: Test-split raw per-example empirical Fisher; B's raw_trace_mean_train256 column is train-only even when repeated on test rows
A finite equal-budget directed probe; existing random and realized-chain directions do not approximate a certified supremum
Task1 and Task5 endpoint-segment integrals; only Task9 S_path is currently measured
Independent training seeds for any population-level or across-seed claim
A shared-head/shared-protection intervention if a pure Task0-geometry causal claim is retained
Exact historical training-source SHA binding; current frozen source/config mapping is adequate for the selected current-visual implementation scope but not bitwise historical-source identity

claims.claim: A compares two inherited Task0 packages under the same future SGD+EWC Task1 rule.
claims.what_results_support: Future optimizer/hyperparameters match, and the RNG receipt matches the new head, sample order, and first-batch image/label hashes over all 51 loader iterations.
claims.what_results_dont_support: The inherited weights, old head, and EWC Fisher differ; A does not isolate geometry or Fisher as a single causal variable.
claims.suggested_claim_revision: Under an audited common future SGD+EWC continuation, the two inherited Task0 packages yield the reported seed0 outcomes.

claims.claim: The GAM Task0 package improves retention and plasticity under fixed future SGD+EWC.
claims.what_results_support: The GAM-origin branch moves 6.69% less and has lower train/subset damage and lower raw trace.
claims.what_results_dont_support: Its a21, a22, and two-task mean are all lower; its signed test CE improvement is also smaller in magnitude.
claims.suggested_claim_revision: For seed0, lower train sensitivity in the inherited GAM package does not guarantee better subsequent class-IL retention or plasticity under common SGD+EWC.

claims.claim: The GAM Task0 anchor has lower sampled train-neighborhood sensitivity in the selected effective-weight coordinates.
claims.what_results_support: Train G and Q95 are lower at every nonzero radius in {0.5,1,2,5,10,20}; GAM/SGD train256 raw-trace ratios range from 0.468 to 0.520 over all measured radii.
claims.what_results_dont_support: This does not cover the test Fisher, continuous balls, worst-case directions, other coordinate systems, or independent training runs.
claims.suggested_claim_revision: On the fixed deterministic train sample and paired random directions, the seed0 GAM anchor shows lower raw gradient energy and sampled positive damage.

claims.claim: GAM lowers neighborhood damage across train and test and generally increases empirical tolerance radius.
claims.what_results_support: Train G/Q95 are favorable and train Q95 tolerance is larger at epsilon 0.001 and 0.05, with the latter right-censored.
claims.what_results_dont_support: Test D_mean and G are higher at all six nonzero radii. All reported test G/Q95 tolerance radii are identical, and all train G tolerance radii are identical.
claims.suggested_claim_revision: The sampled neighborhood benefit is train-split specific; the present test curves and prefix-safe radii do not show a general tolerance advantage.

claims.claim: The neighborhood scan establishes worst-case robustness.
claims.what_results_support: It establishes behavior for 16 paired random directions and realized historical chain directions.
claims.what_results_dont_support: No directed raw-Fisher search or certified supremum was performed; K=16 Q95 and sampled maxima are exploratory finite-set statistics.
claims.suggested_claim_revision: Use sampled-random and finite-directed language; do not use worst-case or supremum language.

claims.claim: The historical sequence's old-task damage ordering cannot be explained by smaller endpoint displacement alone.
claims.what_results_support: At every Task1-Task9 checkpoint, GAM-to-GAM has larger effective-weight displacement and lower Task0 test-local CE change than SGD-to-SGD. At Task9, drift is 1.400472589 versus 1.197584100 and test damage is 0.034347380 versus 0.260130529.
claims.what_results_dont_support: This comparison does not identify which component of the GAM-to-GAM training procedure causes the lower damage.
claims.suggested_claim_revision: In this seed0 historical sequence, displacement magnitude alone does not order old-task damage.

claims.claim: Lower unit-displacement path sensitivity causally mediates the historical chain's lower damage.
claims.what_results_support: At Task9, lower S_path, lower same-sample damage, and larger displacement co-occur; quadrature convergence and D_subset-squared bound checks pass.
claims.what_results_dont_support: Only the Task0-to-Task9 ambient endpoint chord was integrated. It is not the optimization trajectory, and the two full chains use different future optimizers, so causal mediation is not identified.
claims.suggested_claim_revision: At Task9, the historical GAM endpoint chord has lower directional empirical-Fisher sensitivity associated with lower same-sample damage; no optimizer-trajectory or causal-mediation claim is made.

claims.claim: Task0 shaping causes lower sensitivity, larger tolerance, and improved later class-IL performance.
claims.what_results_support: Some train-sensitivity and historical full-sequence directional observations have the anticipated sign.
claims.what_results_dont_support: B-test reverses for G, reported tolerance is not generally larger, A class-IL is worse, and A/B/C do not share one intervention chain.
claims.suggested_claim_revision: Report coordinate-specific sensitivity observations and the negative A/test results as separate findings; do not join them into a causal chain.

coordinate_caveat: All B/C norms, radii, traces, and S_path values use 24 dense effective Q/V matrices with a joint Frobenius metric. Effective weights remove the trivial reciprocal A/B scaling ambiguity, but the measurements remain dependent on layer coordinates and scaling and are not invariant to arbitrary reparameterization. Random dense perturbations can leave the rank-10 LoRA manifold.
path_caveat: C integrates the ambient straight segment between realized endpoints. Intermediate points are not asserted to be optimizer iterates or rank-10 factorized states. The supported term is endpoint-segment sensitivity, not optimization-trajectory sensitivity.
split_caveat: B raw Fisher is train256 only; repeated CSV values on test rows do not create a test Fisher measurement. C's I, S_path, D_subset, and bound check use the same train256 subset, while full-test loss and accuracy are parallel descriptive outcomes and are not used in the bound.
revised_claim_prose: In one ImageNet-A seed of the current visual GAM+EWC implementation, the GAM-trained Task0 anchor exhibits lower raw empirical-Fisher trace and lower sampled positive loss damage on a fixed deterministic Task0 training sample in effective Q/V-weight coordinates. This advantage does not extend to mean positive test-neighborhood damage or to the reported test tolerance radii. Under a paired common SGD+EWC Task1 continuation, inheriting the GAM Task0 state does not improve class-IL accuracy. Separately, in the historical full GAM-to-GAM ten-task chain, old-task loss damage remains lower despite larger endpoint displacement, and the Task0-to-Task9 endpoint segment has lower directional empirical-Fisher sensitivity. These observations show direction-dependent, coordinate-specific sensitivity structure, but do not establish a causal chain from Task0 shaping to later accuracy.
